items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So, we have a pianist named Michael Weiss.

ctx.x: Who else is in the group now?

The pianist that was supposed to make the tour was a pianist named Mickey Tucker, who was with us when we got back together a few years ago, but Mickey lives in Australia. His wife is Australian, and she finally was able to persuade him to come back to live there after living here for some years. But, he has a very serious back problem and he couldn’t make the tour in Europe because he couldn’t get the proper medication, you know traveling around. He sent a fax saying that the people who were booking the tour…

items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: you said Art Farmer used to call you “Veiss” because of his time across the pond.

ctx.x: Michael Weiss has made a significant contribution to jazz as a pianist, composer, and educator. In addition to leading his own ensembles, Michael has played with numerous jazz luminaries, including Johnny Griffin, Art Farmer, and Charles McPherson.
Michael was interviewed via Zoom on December 22, 2021 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
